title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: Mixed anion templates can act cooperatively: strongly coordinating oxoanions build the hydroxo units, while encapsulated halide or perchlorate ions disperse and balance excess positive charge, and changing the anion set can switch the resulting architecture.
explanation: In cage-like Ln27, eight carbonate ions organize cubane, planar-square and hat-like units while one perchlorate occupies the cavity. Replacing the six μ8-perchlorates of cage-like Gd38 with chloride plus nitrate gives barrel-like Gd48; related Er48 uses Cl−/NO3− and Ho48 uses Br−/CO3^2− in analogous layered wheels. The review treats these as evidence that mixed anions both direct self-assembly and charge-balance the core.
scope: Giant lanthanide hydroxide cages and barrels (about Ln27–Ln48) using mixed halide/oxoanion templates.
conditions: Gd38/Gd48 are CAA-supported clusters; Er48 and Ln36 are hydrothermal nicotinate assemblies; Ho48 is hydrothermal from Ho2O3, Mn(OAc)2, isonicotinic acid, formic acid and KBr, with carbonate ascribed to oxidation of formic acid.
caveats: For spherical Ln36 the prose assigns six nitrates to the {Ln24} wheel and two chlorides to the cavity, while the Fig. 12 caption emphasizes six nitrates; template roles should be read with that internal inconsistency.
